question: A study group debates nucleotide excision repair of ultraviolet DNA damage. Which claim is accurate?
options: UV damage is repaired by digesting the entire chromosome.
Sunscreen works by repairing DNA after damage occurs.
UV light strengthens DNA by adding extra bonds.
Nucleotide excision repair removes UV-damaged DNA segments.
gold_answer: Nucleotide excision repair removes UV-damaged DNA segments.
notes: Team-authored original item on nucleotide excision repair of ultraviolet DNA damage. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Sunscreen works by repairing DNA after damage occurs.

claims.text: Repair enzymes cut out the damaged DNA segment.

evidence.text: Excision enzymes nick the strand on both sides of the dimer and remove the damaged patch.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes cutting out the damaged patch, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Excision repair operates only in skin cells.

evidence.text: Nucleotide excision repair operates in essentially all nucleated human cells.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states the repair operates broadly, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Sunscreen makes UV exposure completely safe.

evidence.text: Sunburn rates were compared between sunscreen users and non-users at the beach.

claims.verdict_rationale: Comparing sunburn rates cannot show complete safety, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Nucleotide excision repair removes UV-damaged DNA segments.

claims.text: DNA polymerase fills the gap using the intact strand as template.

evidence.text: After excision, polymerase synthesizes replacement DNA guided by the undamaged complementary strand.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes template-guided gap filling, which entails the claim.

evidence.text: Dimers kink and destabilize the helix, blocking replication until removed.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states dimers destabilize the helix, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: All UV damage leads to cancer.

evidence.text: Cancer outcomes were tracked in participants with measured UV exposure.

claims.verdict_rationale: Tracking outcomes cannot show all damage leads to cancer, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: UV damage is repaired by digesting the entire chromosome.

claims.text: UV light fuses adjacent pyrimidine bases into dimers.

evidence.text: Ultraviolet photons link neighboring thymine or cytosine bases into cyclobutane dimers that distort the helix.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes photon-induced dimer formation, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Repair copies the damaged strand to preserve the mutation.

evidence.text: Repair uses the intact complementary strand as the template, restoring the original sequence.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states the intact strand templates repair, which refutes the claim.

evidence.text: Mutation counts were compared between repair-proficient and repair-deficient cell lines.

claims.verdict_rationale: A comparison of counts cannot show every mutation is prevented, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
